rubrics.evidence: The patch only carves running methods into PolicyRunner; PolicyDefiner remains one exported interface unioning all declaration capabilities (AllowElements/AllowElementsMatching/AllowElementsContent/SkipElementsContent, AllowAttrs/AllowNoAttrs, AllowStyles, AllowURLSchemes/AllowURLSchemesMatching/AllowURLSchemeWithCustomPolicy/RequireParseableURLs/AllowRelativeURLs/RewriteSrc, RequireNoFollowOnLinks/RequireNoFollowOnFullyQualifiedLinks/RequireNoReferrerOnLinks/RequireNoReferrerOnFullyQualifiedLinks/RequireCrossOriginAnonymous/AddTargetBlankToFullyQualifiedLinks/RequireSandboxOnIFrame, AllowComments/AllowDataAttributes/AllowUnsafe/AddSpaceWhenStrippingTag). declareEmailRules still accepts PolicyDefiner, and helpers.go declare* functions are unchanged, so part-dependent rule blocks remain bound to the full declaration surface rather than only the capabilities they use.
rubrics.criterion: The all-in-one policy definer seam in the library core is no longer a single interface that unions unrelated sanitization capabilities (running a policy together with declaring elements, attributes, styles, URL policies, link and iframe hardening, and output toggles): consumers of the policy declaration surface are now bound only to capabilities their role actually uses, whether by focused role interfaces, narrower per-use seams, or use of the concrete policy where no seam is needed.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch only splits PolicyDefiner into PolicyDefiner and PolicyRunner and updates the command-line tools; it contains no changes to policies.go, so ugcConformanceGuard remains in place implementing the full declaration surface with inert discard methods such as AllowElementsMatching, AllowStyles, AllowURLSchemeWithCustomPolicy, RequireSandboxOnIFrame, AllowComments, and AllowUnsafe. UGCPolicy still constructs g := ugcConformanceGuard{p: p} and routes declarations through it, so the guard is still obligated to provide every declaration seam capability it never uses.
rubrics.criterion: The type that stands between the built-in user generated content profile and the concrete policy is no longer obligated to provide every seam capability it never uses: it is either removed, or its remaining surface is narrowed to the capabilities the profile actually applies, and the profile's own hand-written declarations and rule blocks still reach the policy with their rules intact.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch only retypes the two stdin-to-stdout runners to PolicyRunner; it does not modify helpers.go and leaves declareEmailRules(pd bluemonday.PolicyDefiner) unchanged. The split PolicyDefiner still exposes all declaration families (AllowElements, AllowAttrs, AllowStyles, AllowURLSchemes, RequireNoFollowOnLinks, AllowComments, AllowUnsafe, etc.), so the reusable rule blocks and the email rule block still take a parameter carrying every policy declaration capability their role never exercises.
rubrics.criterion: Functions that only declare a group of rules (the reusable helper blocks for standard URLs, standard attributes, styling, images, data URI images, lists, tables and iframes, and the email port's local rule block) and functions that only stream sanitized output (the stdin-to-stdout runners of both command-line tools) no longer take a parameter that also carries the run capability and every policy declaration capability their role never exercises.

Every production call site wired to the all-in-one seam was updated together: the helper-block wrappers still provide their public convenience behaviors, the profile assembly still applies the same rules through the new structure, and no production caller is left constructing, wrapping, or passing the obsolete broad seam type.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not modify helpers.go; the reusable rule-block helpers such as declareStandardURLs, declareStandardAttributes, declareImages, declareLists, declareTables, and declareIFrames retain the same element, attribute, regex, URL, and hardening declarations as before. The patch only splits running methods out of PolicyDefiner into a new PolicyRunner interface in policy.go and updates the command-line runners to use PolicyRunner, without re-authoring the rules inside any block.
rubrics.criterion: The reusable rule-block helpers gained no unnecessary coupling to a particular decomposition: their bodies still declare the same elements, attributes, regex constraints and URL/hardening rules as before, so a profile applying a block gets the identical rule set regardless of how the seam was decomposed.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch changes only cmd/sanitise_html_email/main.go, cmd/sanitise_ugc/main.go, and policy.go; it does not touch policies.go, so the ugcConformanceGuard introduced in the smell remains with its inert discard stubs, e.g. AllowElementsMatching/AllowElementsContent/SkipElementsContent returning g.p, AllowNoAttrs/AllowStyles returning builders that bind nothing, AllowURLSchemesMatching/AllowURLSchemeWithCustomPolicy/RewriteSrc returning g.p, RequireNoFollowOnFullyQualifiedLinks/RequireNoReferrerOnLinks/RequireNoReferrerOnFullyQualifiedLinks/RequireCrossOriginAnonymous/AddTargetBlankToFullyQualifiedLinks returning g.p, and empty RequireSandboxOnIFrame/AllowComments/AllowDataAttributes. These methods exist only to satisfy the broad seam and are not removed or replaced by real behavior.
rubrics.criterion: No discard-stub implementations remain that exist only to satisfy the broad seam: methods whose whole body returns the underlying policy unchanged, returns a builder that binds nothing, or is empty while silently dropping the requested capability, and any guard or wrapper method that exists only because the seam required a capability its owner refuses, are removed or replaced by real behavior.

rubrics.evidence: In policy.go the patch removes Sanitize, SanitizeBytes, SanitizeReader, and SanitizeReaderToWriter from PolicyDefiner and adds a separate PolicyRunner interface containing only those four execution methods. The I/O helpers sanitizeEmailInput and sanitizeInput are changed to accept bluemonday.PolicyRunner and call pr.Sanitize, while declareEmailRules still takes PolicyDefiner. This decomposes the previous union of declaration and execution capabilities into two narrow seams rather than renaming or re-aliasing the broad type.
rubrics.criterion: The broad seam was renamed, re-aliased, or otherwise preserved under a different type name instead of being decomposed: a type still exists (interface or generalization point) whose method set unions the same or nearly the same unrelated declaration and execution capabilities, so the previous coupling persists in new clothing.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only separates running capability from declaration capability: it moves Sanitize/SanitizeBytes/SanitizeReader/SanitizeReaderToWriter out of PolicyDefiner into a new PolicyRunner interface and updates the two tools' runner functions to accept PolicyRunner. It does not modify helpers.go or policies.go, where the UGC profile and reusable rule blocks are declared. In the tools, all declaration calls remain unchanged: cmd/sanitise_html_email still calls declareEmailRules(pd) and p.AllowStyling()/p.AllowDataURIImages() on the concrete policy, and cmd/sanitise_ugc still declares on p before running via pr. No element, attribute, URL scheme, custom URL policy, link hardening, or output toggle is removed, added, or altered, so sanitized output is unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: Sanitization behavior changed: some element, attribute, URL scheme, custom URL policy, link hardening or output toggle that the built-in UGC profile, its rule blocks, or the two tools previously declared is now missing, added or altered, so sanitized output differs for the same input.

rubrics.evidence: The patch does not modify helpers.go, so reusable blocks such as AllowStandardURLs, AllowStandardAttributes, AllowStyling, AllowImages, AllowDataURIImages, AllowLists, AllowTables, and AllowIFrames keep their existing signatures and effects. In policy.go, the run methods are not renamed or re-signatured; they are exposed via a new PolicyRunner interface with identical signatures (Sanitize(s string) string, SanitizeBytes(b []byte) []byte, SanitizeReader(r io.Reader) *bytes.Buffer, SanitizeReaderToWriter(r io.Reader, w io.Writer) error), and *Policy still implements them. The command-line runners switch to PolicyRunner but still call Sanitize on the same concrete policy, preserving behavior.
rubrics.criterion: Public API or documented helper behavior broke: the reusable blocks (AllowStandardURLs, AllowStandardAttributes, AllowStyling, AllowImages, AllowDataURIImages, AllowLists, AllowTables, AllowIFrames), the chain methods they depend on (AllowAttrs with Matching, OnElements, Globally; AllowElements; AllowStyles; AllowURLSchemes), or the run methods (Sanitize, SanitizeBytes, SanitizeReader, SanitizeReaderToWriter) changed name, signature or effect for existing callers.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch only modifies cmd/* and policy.go and does not touch policies.go, so the ugcConformanceGuard from the smell remains in UGCPolicy assembly. Its inert methods still silently discard declarations instead of applying them (e.g., AllowElementsMatching and AllowURLSchemeWithCustomPolicy return g.p unchanged; AllowStyles/AllowNoAttrs return empty builders), leaving a guard in the declaration path that swallows calls.
rubrics.criterion: A rule requested during assembly is silently discarded instead of applied: some shim, adapter, guard or parameter left in the path from a declaration call to the policy swallows the declaration (the way the guarded profile ignored capabilities its profile forbids), so content that should be sanitized passes through unchanged or content that should be kept is stripped.

rubrics.evidence: Both command-line tools preserve their stream contract: main still calls sanitizeEmailInput(pr, os.Stdin, os.Stdout) and sanitizeInput(pr, os.Stdin, os.Stdout) and wraps errors with log.Fatal(err). The runner functions still read all input via io.ReadAll(in), return err on read failure, and write sanitized output via fmt.Fprint(out, pr.Sanitize(string(dirty))). The retyping from PolicyDefiner to PolicyRunner changes only the capability interface, not the stdin/stdout/read-error behavior.
rubrics.criterion: The command-line tools' observable I/O changed: a tool no longer reads all of stdin, no longer writes the sanitized document to stdout, or no longer aborts with its existing log behavior when input cannot be read.
